location: Experiment 2 Results & discussion and General discussion, printed p. 967 (PDF/text p. 8)
quote: backgrounds were more likely to be recalled when ... cued with emotional objects compared to neutral ... objects. These results generally replicated those of ... Mickley Steinmetz et al. (2016), but shed new light on ... the inﬂuence of emotion on associative memory.
reason: Primary source identity is verified (Madan, Knight, Kensinger, & Mickley Steinmetz, 2020, Cognition and Emotion, 34(5), 960-969, DOI 10.1080/02699931.2019.1710110). Although multiple Experiment 2 statistical tests on p. 967 (unconditioned Valence main effect, TargetxValence interaction, positive/negative vs. neutral background-recall t-tests, and conditionalized Valence effect) remain candidates for the numerical statistics, all are significant in the predicted direction and the authors explicitly state that enhanced cued recall of backgrounds cued with emotional versus neutral objects replicated Mickley Steinmetz et al. (2016).
